editorial.headline: Bodies, Trailers, and Custom Vehicle Builds Under KBLI 29200
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 29200 covers the industrial work of building vehicle bodies, trailers, semitrailers, specialist containers, and made-to-order motor-vehicle customisation.
editorial.body:
KBLI 29200 is a manufacturing classification for the built form of road vehicles rather than the complete vehicle as a brand or consumer product. Its centre of gravity is the making of vehicle bodies and bodywork for four-wheeled-or-larger motor vehicles, including specialised bodies for fire engines, mobile libraries, armoured cars, and concrete mixer trucks. The record also brings in seating as part of vehicle-body production, equipment for motor vehicles, trailers, and semitrailers, and the fabrication of chassis or frames for trailers.

The activity is broader than a simple workshop label. It includes trailer and semitrailer manufacturing, with examples such as tankers, enclosed and open-body trailers, and caravans. It also includes custom repair and made-to-order customisation of motor vehicles, plus the manufacture of specially designed containers, including containers for liquid transport, when they are equipped for carriage by one or more modes of transport. In plain English, this is the code for businesses that turn steel, structure, and vehicle engineering into usable transport bodies and towed platforms.

On scale, the record is unusually wide: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification can describe anything from a small bodywork or customisation operation through to a larger industrial manufacturer, provided the registered activity remains inside the scope described here. For founders, that scale range matters because it signals that the code is not reserved only for a large plant, nor limited only to a small artisanal activity. The same KBLI can sit behind several sizes of business, with the activity scope doing the defining work.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. The record lists PMA status as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Bali does not add a separate percentage or ownership cap in this record. The Bali-side status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule itself is still important context: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But this record does not mark KBLI 29200 as blocked in Bali. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record provided.
